title: NZ MBIE Determination 2025/031 (comparative): relocated dwelling and extension on a sloping site, refused consent
jurisdiction: New Zealand (Building Act 2004); Tauranga City Council; comparative only, not Alberta
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992) as cited; E1/VM1 amendment 12 and E1/AS1 first edition amendment 12 as cited; B1/AS1 and B1/VM1 referenced
source_url_note: Building CodeHub resource page for the same MBIE determination (Information provider: MBIE); the building.govt.nz determination page is WAF-blocked for this worker.

facts.text: The determination arises from the authority's refusal to grant building consent for the relocation and alteration of an existing dwelling.
The property generally slopes downhill to the west; the relocated single-storey timber-framed dwelling is about 57 m2 excluding the new deck.
The first refusal reason cited a lack of evidence to mitigate natural hazard on site (slippage) after the earthworks design changed.
The proposed building work includes timber-piled foundations for the relocated dwelling and extension.
Figure 2 is hazard modelling information from the authority.
